cases.sentence: Кити ходила с матерью и с ___, весело щеголявшим в своем европейском, купленном готовым во Франкфурте сюртучке.
cases.explain: «московским полковником» — after the preposition «в», the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: Kitty was walking there with her mother and the Moscow colonel, smart and jaunty in his European coat, bought ready-made at Frankfort. They were walking on one side of the arcade, trying to avoid Levin, who was walking on the other side. Varenka, in her dark dress, in a black hat with a turndown brim, was walking up and down the whole length of the arcade with a blind Frenchwoman, and, every time she met Kitty, they exchanged friendly glances.

cases.sentence: Они ходили по одной стороне галереи, стараясь избегать Левина, ходившего по ___.
cases.explain: «другой стороне» — after the preposition «по», the dative marks the indirect object or recipient.
cases.translation: Kitty was walking there with her mother and the Moscow colonel, smart and jaunty in his European coat, bought ready-made at Frankfort. They were walking on one side of the arcade, trying to avoid Levin, who was walking on the other side. Varenka, in her dark dress, in a black hat with a turndown brim, was walking up and down the whole length of the arcade with a blind Frenchwoman, and, every time she met Kitty, they exchanged friendly glances.

cases.sentence: Варенька в своем темном платье, в черной, с отогнутыми вниз полями шляпе ходила со слепою француженкой во всю длину галереи, и каждый раз, как она встречалась с Кити, они перекидывались ___.
cases.explain: «дружелюбным взглядом» — the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: Kitty was walking there with her mother and the Moscow colonel, smart and jaunty in his European coat, bought ready-made at Frankfort. They were walking on one side of the arcade, trying to avoid Levin, who was walking on the other side. Varenka, in her dark dress, in a black hat with a turndown brim, was walking up and down the whole length of the arcade with a blind Frenchwoman, and, every time she met Kitty, they exchanged friendly glances.

cases.sentence: – Мама, можно мне заговорить с нею? – сказала Кити, следившая за своим ___ и заметившая, что она подходит к ключу и что они могут сойтись у него.
cases.explain: «незнакомым другом» — after the preposition «за», the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: “Mamma, couldn’t I speak to her?” said Kitty, watching her unknown friend, and noticing that she was going up to the spring, and that they might come there together.

cases.sentence: Этот ___ побранился с доктором, наговорил ему дерзости за то, что тот его не так лечит, и замахнулся палкой.
cases.explain: «высокий господин» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “Scandalous and disgraceful!” answered the colonel. “The one thing to be dreaded is meeting Russians abroad. That tall gentleman was abusing the doctor, flinging all sorts of insults at him because he wasn’t treating him quite as he liked, and he began waving his stick at him. It’s simply a scandal!”

cases.sentence: С ___, наблюдая неизвестного своего друга, Кити заметила, что m-lle Варенька и с Левиным и его женщиной находится уже в тех отношениях, как и с другими своими proteges.
cases.explain: «следующего дня» — after the preposition «с», the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: The next day, as she watched her unknown friend, Kitty noticed that Mademoiselle Varenka was already on the same terms with Levin and his companion as with her other protégés. She went up to them, entered into conversation with them, and served as interpreter for the woman, who could not speak any foreign language.

cases.sentence: Она подходила к ним, разговаривала, служила переводчицей для женщины, не умевшей говорить ни на одном ___.
cases.explain: «иностранном языке» — after the preposition «на», for location or topic.
cases.translation: The next day, as she watched her unknown friend, Kitty noticed that Mademoiselle Varenka was already on the same terms with Levin and his companion as with her other protégés. She went up to them, entered into conversation with them, and served as interpreter for the woman, who could not speak any foreign language.

cases.sentence: – Какое вы доброе дело сделали вчера нашему ___! – сказала княгиня.
cases.explain: «жалкому соотечественнику» — the dative marks the indirect object or recipient.
cases.translation: “What a good deed you did yesterday to our poor compatriot!” said the princess.

cases.sentence: – Ну вот, Кити, твое ___ познакомиться с mademoiselle…
cases.explain: «сильное желание» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “Well, see, Kitty, your intense desire to make friends with Mademoiselle. …”

cases.sentence: Кити покраснела от радости и долго молча жала руку своего ___, которая не отвечала на ее пожатие, – но неподвижно лежала в ее руке.
cases.explain: «нового друга» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: Kitty blushed with pleasure, and slowly, without speaking, pressed her new friend’s hand, which did not respond to her pressure, but lay motionless in her hand. The hand did not respond to her pressure, but the face of Mademoiselle Varenka glowed with a soft, glad, though rather mournful smile, that showed large but handsome teeth.
